finding.claim: MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH is not enforced for chunked (no Content-Length) request bodies: data is queued unbounded and the size check runs only after full buffering, or never on the streaming path. Unauthenticated memory/disk exhaustion within BODY_TIMEOUT.
finding.source: Unauthenticated client sends POST/PUT/PATCH with Transfer-Encoding: chunked and no Content-Length on any route (asgi.py:59-72 handle_messages).
finding.sink: Body.put into unbounded asyncio.Queue (request.py:110-111) and multipart streaming to temp files (formparser.py:196-197).

trace.note: Every http.request chunk is put into request.body with no size check
Declared-length check only applies when Content-Length is set
__anext__ performs no size check (streaming path used by multipart parser)
MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH check runs only after the full queue is drained into memory
Multipart parser iterates body chunks and writes file parts to temp storage with no total cap

finding.guards_checked: Declared Content-Length check (request.py:65-70) bypassed by chunked; post-buffer size check (request.py:102-106) does not bound memory; __anext__ (request.py:75-82) unchecked; BODY_TIMEOUT (request.py:288, :359) is time-only. Caveat: content_length returning None for chunked comes from werkzeug, not in repo (wrappers/base.py does not define it).

finding.claim: send_file raises TypeError for every on-disk file because bytes() is called on a pathlib.Path in the etag computation, so static file serving (and send_from_directory/send_file(path)) returns 500 for all existing files. Logic flaw, not a security bypass.
finding.source: Any GET to the default static route <static_url_path>/<path:filename> for an existing file.
finding.sink: adler32(bytes(file_path)) in send_file (helpers.py:348), where file_path is a Path from file_path_to_path (helpers.py:337, utils.py:35-43).

trace.note: safe_join path construction (traversal guard is sound)
is_file check passes for existing file
filename converted to Path via file_path_to_path

finding.guards_checked: safe_join and is_file are present and correct; the defect is the bytes() conversion. Verified by reading plus Python semantics; not executed (no shell available).

finding.claim: Debug/testing error page renders the exception message and frame locals with a Jinja Template that has autoescape disabled, enabling reflected XSS when attacker-controlled text reaches an exception or local.
finding.source: Attacker-controlled request data that ends up in an exception message or a frame local, with app.debug or app.testing enabled.
finding.sink: Template(TEMPLATE).render(...) in traceback_response, emitting value=error (debug.py:59) and frame.locals reprs (debug.py:77-82) unescaped.

trace.note: _handle_exception shows traceback only when app.debug or app.testing
Renders value=error and frame locals into HTML without escaping

finding.guards_checked: No HTML escaping on the template (jinja2 Template default). Gate is operator-set debug/testing mode, hence low severity.
